problem.text: The FP32-input gated activation kernel converted activation(x) * y directly to FP16 without saturation. Products exceeding FP16's finite range could therefore overflow at the output boundary.

reasoning.text: The change clamps the converted half2 pair rather than changing activation evaluation or FP32 multiplication. This confines saturation to the existing FP32-to-FP16 boundary.

impact.text: Both SiLU and GELU FP32-input routes receive the clamp. The FP16-input kernel and standalone PyTorch activations in MLP remain unchanged, so the commit message's scope is broader than the implementation.

source_notes.text: The FP32 activation introduction entry records incompatible in-place FP32 destinations and an odd-element tail omission.

Current source narrows that inherited assessment: BlockSparseMLP now supplies a separate half destination when needed in both ordinary and fused execution. GatedMLP still passes u as its destination, and the paired-kernel tail omission remains. This task changes neither condition.

Issue 55, “Possible GLM4 32B regression,” reports a loading-time int/NoneType comparison failure; issue 31, “TypeError with presence penalty,” reports incompatible sampler arguments. Neither discussion establishes motivation for this activation clamp. The inspected overlap with issue 55 is the mlp.py pathname, not a matching activation failure.

limitations: No CUDA compilation, repository kernel execution, numerical accuracy evaluation or performance measurement was performed.
The scalar model uses Python arithmetic and explicit overflow substitution; it does not reproduce CUDA approximate activation instructions or establish CUDA min/max behavior for NaNs.
Whole-tree literal searches establish the inspected internal callers, not dynamically selected or external consumers.

chapters.title: Saturate FP32 gated activations at the FP16 output boundary

claims.text: act_mul_kernel_f loads float2 gate and up values, evaluates the selected activation on the gate lanes, multiplies by the up lanes in float, and converts the pair with __float22half2_rn. The new clamp_half2_to_finite then applies an upper and lower half2 bound before storage. It clamps the gated product, not the activation alone.

The bounds ±65504 are the finite binary16 endpoints: (2 − 2^-10) × 2^15 = 65504. A standard-library scalar model produced SiLU products ±1000000, modeled their half conversion as ±infinity, and saturated them to ±65504; an ordinary small product retained its rounded half value.

Saturation trades the magnitude of out-of-range products for a bounded FP16 value. Its placement preserves FP32 intermediates until conversion rather than clipping gate or up projections earlier; improved downstream stability is a plausible consequence, not a measured result.

silu_mul and gelu_mul dispatch on x.dtype(), require matching input dtypes and always require a half destination. Their FP32 branches share the changed kernel; half branches still use the unchanged half2 multiplication. The new helper is called only from act_mul_kernel_f.

Whole-tree searches locate extension activation selection in GatedMLP and BlockSparseMLP. BlockSparseMLP's ordinary expert path uses a half temporary for non-half intermediates; its fully quantized single-token path uses the half interm_a buffer. Both feed that result to the down projection. GatedMLP instead calls activation(g, u, u), retaining the incompatible FP32-destination case. Plain MLP uses PyTorch activation functions and does not reach this clamp.

findings.description: GatedMLP retains an in-place destination incompatible with the extension's FP32-input contract.
findings.trigger: GatedMLP gate/up projections produce FP32 tensors.
findings.expected_behavior: Provide a half activation destination so execution can reach the clamped FP32-input kernel.
findings.actual_behavior: GatedMLP.forward passes FP32 u as z; the wrapper's half-destination check rejects it before launch. BlockSparseMLP's inspected ordinary and fused paths avoid this mismatch.

verification.description: Compared searched activation callers with wrapper dtype validation and the task's kernel-only change.
verification.limits: Conditional on FP32 projection outputs; no model execution.

findings.description: Both paired activation kernels still omit an odd final element.
findings.trigger: An exported activation receives otherwise suitable buffers with odd numel; GatedMLP exposes configurable padding that can permit odd intermediate lengths.
findings.expected_behavior: Write activation(x) * y to every output element.
findings.actual_behavior: The numel/2 guard processes complete pairs only. The final destination element remains untouched; the clamp does not repair coverage.

verification.description: Enumerated the 256-thread, two-elements-per-thread launch and guard. Lengths 1, 3, 129 and 513 each left their final element unwritten; 128 and 512 were fully covered.
verification.limits: Integer coverage model only, not CUDA execution; ordinarily padded internal buffers can avoid this trigger.

annotation.summary: Clamps FP32-input SiLU/GELU gated products to finite FP16 bounds after conversion. Half-input execution is unchanged, and inherited destination and odd-tail limitations remain.

argv:
import struct, math
m=struct.unpack('<e',bytes.fromhex('ff7b'))[0]
print('binary16 maximum:',m,'formula:',(2-2**-10)*2**15)
for x,y in [(1000.,1000.),(1000.,-1000.),(1.,2.)]:
 p=x/(1+math.exp(-x))*y
 try: h=struct.unpack('<e',struct.pack('<e',p))[0]
 except OverflowError: h=math.copysign(math.inf,p)
 print('scalar SiLU product',p,'half model',h,'clamped',max(-m,min(h,m)))
for n in (1,3,128,129,512,513):
 written=[i for t in range(((n+511)//512)*256) if t<n//2 for i in (2*t,2*t+1)]
 print(n,'unwritten',sorted(set(range(n))-set(written)))
